import.title: Import staff from a spreadsheet
import.columnsHelp: Needed: first_name, last_name, email. Optional: employment (full-time, part-time, casual, on call, volunteer), positions (separated by ;), roles (staff, head lifeguard, supervisor, front desk, hr, steward), hire_date and date_of_birth (YYYY-MM-DD), employee_number, phone, language (en or fr), union_member (yes/no). French column names work too. roles also accepts employee (general city worker) and your city's own role names.
import.sendInvites: Email each new person an invitation to set their password
import.skipNote: Rows to fix are skipped. Fix them in the file and import again; people already added won't be duplicated.

people.fairProcessHelp: A suspension or termination needs each of these. They're recorded with the time you confirmed them.

checks.factsReviewed: I reviewed the facts attached and they are accurate and complete.
checks.protectedGrounds: None of this relates to a protected ground (disability, family status, pregnancy, religion and others) or protected leave, and I considered whether accommodation is owed.
checks.employeeHeard: The employee was told the concerns and had a fair chance to respond.
checks.agreementChecked: The steps in our policy and collective agreement were followed.
checks.stewardOffered: A union steward was offered for the meeting.
checks.counselReviewed: Cause, notice and severance were reviewed with legal counsel or the HR lead.

people.attachFacts: Tick at least one fact this decision relies on.
people.myFileHelp: Everything your managers see about your attendance and conduct. You can respond to any record.
people.addResponseHelp: Your account is kept with the record and shown to anyone who reads it. You can add it once.
people.responseSaved: Your response is on the record.
how: Your attendance score starts at 100 and covers the last 90 days. Late clock-ins, missed shifts and giving away a shift with under 24 hours' notice lower it; picking up shifts raises it.
Sick days and protected leave never count. A supervisor can excuse anything else with a reason, and the reason stays visible to you.
Supervisors can add notes about your work, including commendations. You're notified each time and see exactly what they wrote.

The score and notes only help managers notice when a conversation may help. Nothing schedules, disciplines or ends your employment automatically; a person decides, and you can always respond in writing.
Every time a manager opens your file, it's logged. You can ask HR to correct anything inaccurate, and you have a right to see the information held about you.
people.skipsSteps: This skips steps in progressive discipline. Say in the summary why (for example, how serious the safety breach was), or choose an earlier step.

deck.title: Rotation
deck.description: Who is on which chair, when they move, and who needs a break. Every move is logged.
deck.rotationMinutesHint: How long a guard stays on one station before moving on. Often 20 to 30 minutes.
deck.maxOnChairHint: Continuous time on stations before a guard must come off for a break.
deck.stationsHelp: Chairs and positions, in the order the rotation moves through them.
deck.noStationsHelp: A supervisor adds the chairs and positions in Settings, Pools.
deck.stationNameHint: For example: Deep end chair, Slide tower, Roving.
deck.orderHint: Guards move from lower numbers to higher. The first station gets the most-rested guard.
deck.rotated: Rotated. Everyone has been moved along.
deck.closed: Deck closed. The rotation log is complete.
deck.nextHelp: Everyone moves one station along every {{m}} minutes; the most-rested guard comes on.
deck.noRelief: Needs a break but nobody is free to relieve them: {{names}}.
deck.onDutyHelp: Clocked in here. Anyone on deck {{m}} minutes in a row needs a break.
deck.onBreak: You're on break from the chair.

compliance.title: Compliance at any minute
compliance.description: Rebuild what the deck looked like at a past moment: who was working and where, their certifications then, staffing against the bather count, chemistry and incidents. Every report is logged.
compliance.pick: Choose a facility and a moment
compliance.pickHelp: For an inspector, an insurer, an inquiry or your own review.
compliance.noIssues: Everyone was certified, staffing met the bather count, and chemistry was in range.

issue.UNDERSTAFFED: Fewer guards on station than the bather count required: {{detail}}
issue.NO_RECENT_CHEMISTRY: No chemistry reading in the 6 hours before: {{detail}}

compliance.noRotation: No rotation was logged at this moment, so stations aren't shown.
compliance.nobody: Nobody was scheduled or clocked in.
compliance.noHeadcount: No headcount in the 3 hours before.
compliance.chem: Chemistry at {{time}}: free chlorine {{fc}} ppm, pH {{ph}}
compliance.noChem: No chemistry reading in the 6 hours before.
compliance.incidentsHelp: Type and time only. Reports stay sealed; opening one asks for a reason and is logged.
compliance.footer: Built from the schedule, timeclock, rotation log, certification records, headcounts and chemistry log as recorded at the time. This report's creation is recorded in the audit log.

access.help: Switch any menu item on or off for each access level in this city. Switching an item off also removes the access only that screen uses, so the app refuses it too. Changes apply on people's next action; every change is logged in the city's audit trail.
access.resetDone: {{role}} is back to the standard access.
access.advancedHelp: Fine-grained control over what each access level can do. Shaded cells differ from the standard. Sensitive permissions reach pay, personal records, discipline or city setup.

onboarding.title: Onboarding
onboarding.description: Everything a new person needs before and after their first shift, split between HR, their supervisor and themselves. Checks and training can be required per position.
onboarding.allDone: Everyone's onboarding is up to date
onboarding.allDoneHelp: New people appear here with what HR, their supervisor and they still need to do.
onboarding.checklistHelp: Items with a lock must be done before this person can be scheduled for that position.
onboarding.waiveHelp: Only HR can waive an item. The reason stays on file.
onboarding.checkHelp: Record the date you saw the check and that it met the position's standard. Do not record the result or keep a copy here.
onboarding.noteHint: Facts only, for example "certificate seen". Never the check result, a SIN or banking details.
onboarding.privacy: For background checks and identity documents, the app keeps only that they were seen, when, by whom and when they expire. Results, copies, SINs and banking details stay out of it.
onboarding.minorsTitle: Works with children or vulnerable people
onboarding.minorsHelp: Switch on for positions such as swim instructors, camp staff and program leaders. It requires a vulnerable sector check, child protection training and HIGH FIVE.
onboarding.byPositionHelp: Switch each item on for the positions that need it. Items marked for everyone apply to all staff. A lock means the item must be done before scheduling.
onboarding.validityHint: Leave blank if it never expires.
onboarding.policyTextHint: For policies: what the employee reads before acknowledging.
onboarding.blocksLabel: Must be done before the person can be scheduled
onboarding.legend: Built in: offer letter, TD1, direct deposit, identity, emergency contact, criminal record and vulnerable sector checks, child protection, HIGH FIVE, WHMIS, health and safety awareness, accessible customer service, policies, orientation, emergency plan, equipment, shadow shifts and skills check. Add your own.
onboarding.readHelp: Read the policy, then type your name to confirm you read it.
onboarding.typeNameHint: This records that you read the policy, with today's date.
onboarding.affected_one: {{count}} person in this position can’t be scheduled until HR records it.
onboarding.affected_other: {{count}} people in this position can’t be scheduled until HR records it.
onboarding.othersOpen_one: HR or your supervisor has {{count}} more item to finish.
onboarding.othersOpen_other: HR or your supervisor have {{count}} more items to finish.

overtime.title: Overtime
overtime.description: Overtime offered in the order your collective agreement sets: fewest hours charged this period first, then seniority. Accepted overtime is recorded automatically; record phone call-outs here.
overtime.orderHelp: Charged since {{date}}. Ties go to the more senior person.
overtime.callHelp: What happened when you offered the overtime. Refusals and unanswered calls count as charged hours if your policy says so.
overtime.policyHelp: How overtime is equalized in your collective agreement.
overtime.clauseHint: Shown with every warning, so supervisors know which rule applies.
overtime.countRefusals: Charge refused and unanswered offers as if worked
overtime.note: Warnings appear before overtime goes to someone out of order. They inform the decision; a supervisor still decides, and every override is logged.
overtime.skips_one: This skips {{count}} person ahead in the overtime order
overtime.skips_other: This skips {{count}} people ahead in the overtime order

brand.motto: Every shift covered. Every person cared for. Every need met.

care.title: Care after incidents
care.description: After a rescue, an ambulance call or a staff injury, everyone involved is offered a private check-in, your support details and time away from the chair. Only that care was offered and followed up is kept.
care.toCheckHelp: A short private conversation within a day. Nothing you discuss is recorded here.
care.none: Nobody needs a check-in right now
care.noneHelp: When a serious incident is reported, the people involved appear here.
care.recorded: Recorded. Thank you for looking out for them.
care.closed_one: {{count}} follow-up closed in the last 30 days.
care.closed_other: {{count}} follow-ups closed in the last 30 days.
care.supportHelp: Shown to staff after a critical incident.
care.eapHint: For example your EFAP phone number, hours and website, or a peer-support contact.
care.privacy: Check-ins record only that they were offered and followed up, by whom and when, never what was said.
care.mineBody: What happened can stay with people. You don't have to handle it alone. A supervisor will check in with you, and you can reach confidential support any time.
care.askBreak: I'd like time off the chair
care.breakSent: Your supervisor has been told. Take the time you need.

accommodation.title: Work restrictions
accommodation.help: Accommodation and return-to-work limits the scheduler enforces. Supervisors see only that a shift is outside this person's restrictions.
accommodation.addHelp: Record the limits only. Never record a diagnosis or medical details here.
accommodation.label: Label
accommodation.labelHint: A general label, for example "Return to work" or "Family responsibilities".
accommodation.saved: Saved. The schedule now respects these limits.
accommodation.privacy: Only HR sees these details, and every view is logged. The employee sees their own restrictions.
accommodation.mineHelp: Agreed with HR. The schedule won't book you outside these.
